Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3226 (102)

CAPESIZE
After a brief mid-week pause in the Pacific due to the Singapore holiday, the second half of the week on C5 has resumed with renewed activity and stronger sentiment. The BCI 182 5TC rose by a further $2,224 to $50,041, with strength evident across both major basins. C5 advanced by 0.555 to $16.870, while C3 gained 0.423 to settle at $37.791. In the Pacific, volumes remained healthy with all three major miners active alongside a decent flow of operator-controlled cargoes and a couple of fresh tenders. The increased activity translated into firmer sentiment throughout the day. Offers on C5 were reportedly opening above $17.00, although miners initially fixed in the mid-$16s before an operator followed at $16.75. There was also market talk of a fixture concluded at a tick above $17.00, although details remained sketchy. The Atlantic continued to build momentum, with firmer sentiment emerging as both rates and activity improved. Following yesterday's focus on the South Atlantic and North Atlantic, stronger fixtures continued to surface across both basins. A particularly strong Transatlantic fixture helped propel the C8 index up by $4,844 to $54,938. On C3, a $37.50 fixture established the benchmark, with bids today reported around $37.50 against offers closer to $38.50. With all three C5 miners active, healthy Pacific volumes, and the Atlantic showing increasingly convincing signs of strength, the market closes on a firm note with positive momentum carrying into the final trading day of the week.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market today is said to be more evenly balanced for the most part, with tonnage and cargo largely matched. Market sources note that despite this general supply demand balance, the tonnage list opening in the North Continent continues to grow, although this has yet to translate into any meaningful rate movement. Reported fronthaul fixtures have remained notable, however, as was the case yesterday it is said that a degree of rate disparity persists between the prompt and further forward stems. With earlier arriving tonnage coming under pressure, owners have been forced to revise their rate ideas down accordingly. In the Pacific, brokers have highlighted the positive sentiment and upward price movement once again which is supported by the multiple fixtures reported. Australian and Indonesian demand remains strong on the prompt side, with concluded rates continuing to edge higher. Both the BBG Tieshan (81,577 2020) open Zhanjiang prompt and the MSXT Emily (85,268 2022) open Lianyungang prompt fixed Australian rounds at around $25,000 - $26,000 region. The scrubber fitted Chiara Oldendorff (98,714 2013) open in Mizushima 2 June fixed for a trip via Australia at $28,250 to Messrs Tongli, whilst the Shun Chang (93,322 2010) open Hong Kong 2/3 June was reported to have fixed a Pacific round at $25,000 but no further details emerged. It has been noted, however, that North Pacific trades have so far failed to achieve comparable levels to Australian business, though some market participants suggest this gap could change. The P5TC improved today by $349 to conclude at $20,978 with a significant weighting for this improvement coming from the Pacific indices.
SUPRAMAX
The general pattern continued today as the Atlantic remained firm whilst the Asian arena lost further ground. The US Gulf still saw a good amount of fresh cargoes brokers said and demand remained certainly for trans Atlantic runs. The Continent-Mediterranean and the South Atlantic remained finely balanced but fixing information remained lacking. The 11TC average was up $95 at $19,835.

Atlantic
The Baoshan Glory (56,686 2012) open Diliskelesi 12/18 June was heard to have been placed on subjects for a trip via Ukraine redelivery at SE Asia in the high teens.

Asia
The Porto Kioni (56,025 2013) was heard to have been placed on subjects for a trip delivery Kandla redelivery Far East with salt at $11,000. The APJ Shirin (56,594 2012) open Mumbai 29 May/3 June fixed via WC India redelivery AG-UAE with intention slag at $16,000 to Graincom.

HANDYSIZE
The Handy market experienced another mixed day, with sentiment largely shaped by positional dynamics. In the Continent and Mediterranean, conditions changed little and the market appeared balanced. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic was notably quiet, with limited reported activity, and rates continued to soften. In contrast, the US Gulf market maintained its upward momentum. Participants remained cautiously optimistic as rates strengthened further, supporting an overall positive outlook for the region. A 40,000-dwt vessel, open in the US Gulf on 1/4 June was fixed for a trip inter Caribbean at $23,000, although further details were not disclosed. In Asia, the market remained healthy following several strong fixtures reported yesterday, which kept sentiment firm. Reflecting these regional variations, the 7TC index rose by $60 to close at $15,254.

Market Fundamentals
China Issues Fresh Urea Export Guidance

China has issued fresh export quotas for urea exports, though these remain unconfirmed by official sources, Reuters reports. The country banned exports of many categories in March to protect domestic farmers from rising prices following the de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Urea exports are managed by a quota system and multiple producers confirmed receipt of quota allocations as of 27 May. Price floors have been set at $660/t FOB for prilled urea, $670/t FOB for granular grade, and $680/t FOB for India-destined prills, CRU reports. While the total allocation has not been officially disclosed, market consensus reported by CRU puts the first-round volume at ~3 Mt: 1.6 Mt for producers, 0.8 Mt for distributors with commercial reserve commitments, 0.4 Mt for government-to-government aid, and 0.2 Mt for major phosphate producers The quotas are particularly significant for India, which sourced over 40% of its urea and diammonium phosphate from the Middle East last year. Domestically, urea prices rebounded following the release of allocations, reversing recent declines as downstream demand picked up. Mainstream prilled prices in Shandong, Henan, and Hebei provinces are now reported at RMB1,760-1,800/t ($260-265/t) EXW, with the low-end up RMB50/t ($7/t) and the high-end reflecting an increase of RMB70/t ($10/t) compared to the week prior, CRU reports

ai_analysis.summary: 2026年5月28日波罗的海干散货指数全线上扬，BDI报3226点上涨102点，其中海岬型领涨245点至5517点。太平洋市场活跃，三大矿商均有出货，C5航线突破17美元关口，大西洋跨大西洋航线C8暴涨4844美元至54938美元。巴拿马型跟随走强25美元至20978美元，太平洋澳洲印尼需求支撑明显。超灵便型与灵便型涨幅有限，市场呈现明显分化特征。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 干散货市场结构性分化明显：海岬型凭借太平洋矿商活跃出货强势领涨，大西洋航线同步走强；巴拿马型太平洋需求支撑价格上扬，但北大西洋运力略显过剩；超灵便型亚洲市场继续走软，大西洋保持坚挺；灵便型美湾持续上升但南大西洋偏弱。整体市场情绪偏暖但结构性分化延续。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 看涨信号：1）C5突破17美元三大矿商参与；2）C8暴涨4844美元大西洋动能强劲；3）P5TC涨349美元太平洋贡献主要权重；4）澳洲航线成交$25,000-26,000区间；5）FFA 6月合同走强至22,200。看跌信号：1）Capesize远期曲线Q3后明显贴水；2）北太平洋未能跟随澳洲航线涨幅；3）Supramax亚洲端持续承压。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 近期焦点：1）Capesize C5能否站稳17美元为本周关键；2）大西洋跨大西洋航线(C8)强势能否延续；3）巴拿马型FFA 6月合同在22,000-22,200区间反复争夺显示多空博弈；4）关注6月运力消化情况及远期曲线结构演变；5）铁矿石价格走稳对运费支撑力度。
